name: Session affinity, Ingress & manual endpoints
objective: CKAD › Services & Networking. Drill every Service shape and the Ingress/endpoints surface: ClusterIP with named targetPort, NodePort on a pinned port, headless, ExternalName, sessionAffinity, Ingress (pathType/ingressClassName/TLS), a selector-less Service + manual EndpointSlice, and a no-hint 'no endpoints' diagnose-fix. Graded exactly.

questions.title: Session affinity
questions.teach:
`sessionAffinity: ClientIP` pins each client IP to the same pod (sticky sessions). Tune the stickiness window with `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds`.

**Gotcha:** the timeout lives under `sessionAffinityConfig`, not directly on `sessionAffinity`.
questions.prompt:
Create a ClusterIP Service `web-sa` for `app=web` on port 80 with **ClientIP session affinity** and a timeout of **3600** seconds.

Target: `web-sa` has `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` and `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds: 3600`.
questions.eli5:
Normally a Service spreads calls across pods like a receptionist handing each new caller to whoever's free — so your second request might land on a totally different pod than your first. **Session affinity** is telling the receptionist: *"once you connect this caller to someone, keep sending that same caller back to the same person."* Sticky sessions.

With `sessionAffinity: ClientIP`, Kubernetes remembers each client's **IP address** and routes it to the same pod it used last time. Handy when a pod holds some in-memory state for a user and you don't want them bounced around.

How long does the receptionist remember? That's the **timeout**. Here it's **3600 seconds** (one hour) of inactivity before the stickiness expires. And that timeout lives in its own sub-section: `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds`.

**Watch out for:**

- The timeout is **not** a field directly on `sessionAffinity`. It nests under **`sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds`** — two levels down. Putting it anywhere else silently does nothing.
- Affinity is by **client IP**, not by user or cookie. If many clients sit behind one NAT/proxy IP, they all stick to the same pod — and a client whose IP changes loses its stickiness.
- The only valid values for `sessionAffinity` are `ClientIP` and `None` (the default). There's no cookie-based option at the Service level (that's an Ingress feature).
- Set *both* pieces: `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` **and** the config block. One without the other isn't what the task asks for.
questions.deepDive:
## Service session affinity — full rundown

### Mental model
By default a Service load-balances each new connection across pods. **`sessionAffinity: ClientIP`** makes kube-proxy route all traffic from a given **source IP** to the **same pod** (sticky sessions), with a configurable idle **timeout** under `sessionAffinityConfig`.

### Create it
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: web-sa, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  selector: { app: web }
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 80 } ]
  sessionAffinity: ClientIP
  sessionAffinityConfig:
    clientIP:
      timeoutSeconds: 3600
```

### The two fields
| Field | Values / default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sessionAffinity` | `None` (default) \| `ClientIP` | enable stickiness |
| `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds` | default **10800** (3h); max 86400 | idle seconds before affinity resets |

> The timeout is **nested** under `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP` — not a sibling of `sessionAffinity`.

### How it behaves
- Routing key is the **client source IP**, hashed to a pod.
- The mapping is refreshed on activity; after `timeoutSeconds` idle, the next connection may pick a new pod.
- Scaling or losing the chosen pod re-hashes affected clients.

### Verify
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get svc web-sa -o jsonpath='{.spec.sessionAffinity}{"\n"}'          # ClientIP
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get svc web-sa \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds}{"\n"}'                 # 3600
```

### ClientIP affinity vs cookie affinity
| | Where | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` | **Service** (kube-proxy) | source IP |
| cookie-based stickiness | **Ingress** controller (annotations) | HTTP cookie |

The Service only offers IP-based affinity; cookie stickiness is an Ingress/controller feature, not a core Service field.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`timeoutSeconds` lives under `sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP`**, not directly on `sessionAffinity`. Misplacing it is silently ignored.
- Only `ClientIP` and `None` are valid for `sessionAffinity`.
- Affinity is **per source IP** — clients behind a shared NAT all land on one pod; a client whose IP changes loses stickiness.
- Default timeout is **10800s**; set it explicitly when a value is required.
- Set **both** the mode and the config if the task specifies a timeout.

### Quick reference
```yaml
spec:
  sessionAffinity: ClientIP
  sessionAffinityConfig: { clientIP: { timeoutSeconds: 3600 } }
```
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get svc web-sa \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds}'
```

questions.title: Ingress with pathType, class, and TLS
questions.teach:
An **Ingress** routes HTTP(S) to Services by host/path. Three fields here: `ingressClassName` picks the controller, each path's `pathType`, and `tls` to terminate HTTPS with a tls Secret.

**Gotcha:** `pathType` is required on every path — omitting it is rejected.
questions.prompt:
Create an Ingress `web-ing` in `svcnet-learn`:
- `ingressClassName: nginx`
- host `myapp.local`, one path `/` with `pathType: Prefix` → Service `web-svc` port `80`
- TLS for host `myapp.local` using secret `web-tls`

Target: `web-ing` has ingressClassName nginx, the Prefix `/` rule to web-svc:80, and a tls entry with secretName web-tls.
questions.hint: Set `spec.ingressClassName: nginx`, a rule with `pathType: Prefix` and `backend.service.name: web-svc` / `port.number: 80`, and `spec.tls: [{hosts: [myapp.local], secretName: web-tls}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: { name: web-ing, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls: [ { hosts: [ myapp.local ], secretName: web-tls } ]
  rules:
  - host: myapp.local
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend: { service: { name: web-svc, port: { number: 80 } } }
YAML

verification.description: web-ing: class nginx, Prefix / -> web-svc:80, TLS secret web-tls

questions.eli5:
A Service gets traffic *inside* the building; an **Ingress** is the smart receptionist at the **front entrance** who reads the address on each visitor's request — the website name (host) and the path like `/` or `/shop` — and sends them to the right internal desk (Service). It's how outside web traffic reaches your apps by friendly URLs instead of raw ports.

This Ingress `web-ing` sets up three things:

- **ingressClassName: nginx** — which receptionist (which Ingress controller) should handle this. A cluster can run several; this picks the nginx one.
- A **rule**: for host `myapp.local`, any path starting with `/` (that's `pathType: Prefix`) goes to Service `web-svc` on port `80`.
- **TLS**: for `myapp.local`, decrypt HTTPS using the certificate stored in Secret `web-tls`. The receptionist handles the padlock so your Service doesn't have to.

**Watch out for:**

- **`pathType` is required on every path.** The three values are `Prefix` (path starts with this), `Exact` (matches exactly), and `ImplementationSpecific`. Omit it and the Ingress is rejected.
- The TLS **`secretName` must point to an existing Secret** of type `kubernetes.io/tls` holding the cert+key; the `hosts` in the tls entry should match the rule's host.
- Without a matching `ingressClassName` (or a default class), no controller picks up the Ingress and nothing routes — it just sits there.
- The backend points at a **Service**, not a pod: `backend.service.name` + `port.number`. That Service must exist and have endpoints for traffic to actually land.
- Host and path matching is literal — `myapp.local` won't match `www.myapp.local`.
questions.deepDive:
## Ingress with pathType, class, and TLS — full rundown

### Mental model
An **Ingress** is an L7 (HTTP/HTTPS) routing rule set: it maps `host` + `path` to backend **Services**. It does nothing on its own — an **Ingress controller** (e.g. ingress-nginx) selected by `ingressClassName` watches Ingress objects and programs the actual proxy. TLS termination happens at the controller using a referenced Secret.

### Create it
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: { name: web-ing, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
  - hosts: [ myapp.local ]
    secretName: web-tls
  rules:
  - host: myapp.local
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: web-svc
            port:
              number: 80
```

### The three required/notable fields
| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ingressClassName` | which controller handles this Ingress |
| `rules[].http.paths[].pathType` | **required** per path |
| `tls[]` | HTTPS termination: `hosts` + `secretName` |

### pathType values
| pathType | Matches |
|---|---|
| `Prefix` | URL path split on `/`, element-wise prefix (`/` matches everything) |
| `Exact` | the path exactly (case-sensitive) |
| `ImplementationSpecific` | up to the controller |

> `pathType` is **mandatory** in `networking.k8s.io/v1`; omitting it fails validation.

### The TLS Secret
Must be type `kubernetes.io/tls` with `tls.crt` + `tls.key`:
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn create secret tls web-tls --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key
```
`tls[].hosts` should match the rule host; the controller presents this cert for `myapp.local`.

### Backend shape (v1 API)
```yaml
backend:
  service:
    name: web-svc
    port: { number: 80 }     # or name: http
```
> Old `extensions/v1beta1` used `serviceName`/`servicePort` — **do not** use on the exam; it's `backend.service.name` + `port.number`.

### Verify
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get ingress web-ing
kubectl -n svcnet-learn describe ingress web-ing
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get ingress web-ing -o jsonpath='{.spec.ingressClassName}{"\n"}'
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get ingress web-ing \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.rules[0].http.paths[0].pathType}{"\n"}'
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`pathType` required on every path** — the most common Ingress validation failure.
- Use the **v1** API and `backend.service.name`/`port.number`, not the beta `serviceName`/`servicePort`.
- `ingressClassName` must match an installed `IngressClass` (or set the default-class annotation) or no controller acts.
- TLS `secretName` must reference an existing `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret; mismatched `hosts` → cert not served for that host.
- Backend is a **Service** (needing live endpoints), not a pod.
- Host/path matching is literal; `myapp.local` ≠ subdomains.

### Quick reference
```yaml
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls: [ { hosts: [ myapp.local ], secretName: web-tls } ]
  rules:
  - host: myapp.local
    http:
      paths:
      - { path: /, pathType: Prefix,
          backend: { service: { name: web-svc, port: { number: 80 } } } }
```

questions.title: Selector-less Service + manual EndpointSlice
questions.teach:
A Service with **no selector** gets no automatic endpoints — you supply them yourself with an **EndpointSlice**. This fronts an external or hand-managed backend.

**Gotcha:** the slice attaches via its `kubernetes.io/service-name: <svc>` label, not a reference field.
questions.prompt:
Create a selector-less ClusterIP Service `ext-svc` (port 80), and an **EndpointSlice** attaching it to a backend at `10.40.0.9:80`.

Target: `ext-svc` has no selector, and an EndpointSlice labelled `kubernetes.io/service-name=ext-svc` with endpoint address `10.40.0.9`.
questions.hint: Service with `ports` and NO `selector`. EndpointSlice (`discovery.k8s.io/v1`) with `metadata.labels.kubernetes.io/service-name: ext-svc`, `addressType: IPv4`, `endpoints: [{addresses: [10.40.0.9]}]`, `ports: [{port: 80}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: ext-svc, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 80 } ]
---
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
kind: EndpointSlice
metadata:
  name: ext-svc-1
  namespace: svcnet-learn
  labels: { kubernetes.io/service-name: ext-svc }
addressType: IPv4
ports: [ { name: "", port: 80 } ]
endpoints: [ { addresses: [ "10.40.0.9" ] } ]
YAML
questions.eli5:
Usually a Service finds its own staff automatically: you give it a `selector` (like "anyone wearing an `app=web` badge") and Kubernetes keeps a live list of matching pods behind it. But sometimes the thing you want to send traffic to **isn't a pod at all** — maybe it's a database running on an old server outside the cluster. There are no badges to match.

So you build a Service with **no selector**. Now Kubernetes won't auto-fill the staff list, because it has no idea who belongs. You supply the list **by hand** using an **EndpointSlice** — a little object that says "here are the real addresses behind this Service": `10.40.0.9` on port `80`.

The clever part: the EndpointSlice doesn't have a "belongs to" field. Instead it attaches to the Service through a **label**: `kubernetes.io/service-name: ext-svc`. Kubernetes reads that label to know this slice is the backing list for `ext-svc`.

**Watch out for:**

- The glue is the **label** `kubernetes.io/service-name=<service>`, not a reference field. Get the label name or value wrong and the slice floats free — the Service still shows no endpoints.
- The Service must have **no selector** (but keep its `ports`). If it had a selector, Kubernetes would manage endpoints itself and ignore/fight your manual ones.
- Use the modern **EndpointSlice** (`discovery.k8s.io/v1`), not the legacy `Endpoints` object. Set `addressType` (e.g. `IPv4`), an `endpoints` list of addresses, and a `ports` list.
- The Service's port and the slice's port should line up so traffic actually reaches `10.40.0.9:80`.
- These addresses are unmanaged — nothing health-checks them. If the external host dies, Kubernetes won't notice.
questions.deepDive:
## Selector-less Service + manual EndpointSlice — full rundown

### Mental model
A Service with a **selector** gets its endpoints managed automatically. A Service with **no selector** is a stable VIP/DNS name whose backends **you** define — by creating an **EndpointSlice** that attaches to the Service via the label `kubernetes.io/service-name: <svc>`. This fronts external or hand-managed backends.

### Create both
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: ext-svc, namespace: svcnet-learn }
spec:
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 80 } ]     # NO selector
---
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
kind: EndpointSlice
metadata:
  name: ext-svc-1
  namespace: svcnet-learn
  labels:
    kubernetes.io/service-name: ext-svc         # <-- the link to the Service
addressType: IPv4                               # IPv4 | IPv6 | FQDN
ports:
- name: ""                                      # must match the Service port name ("" if unnamed)
  port: 80
endpoints:
- addresses: [ "10.40.0.9" ]
```

### How the slice binds to the Service
| Mechanism | Field |
|---|---|
| **Which Service** | label `kubernetes.io/service-name: <svc>` |
| Address family | `addressType: IPv4 / IPv6 / FQDN` |
| Backend IPs | `endpoints[].addresses` |
| Ports | `ports[]` (name must align with Service port name) |

> There is **no** `serviceName` field — the label is the only link.

### EndpointSlice vs legacy Endpoints
| | `Endpoints` (v1 core) | **`EndpointSlice`** (discovery.k8s.io/v1) |
|---|---|---|
| Status | legacy | current/preferred |
| Scale | one object, grows unbounded | sharded into slices |
| Exam | may appear | prefer EndpointSlice |

Legacy equivalent (still works):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Endpoints
metadata: { name: ext-svc, namespace: svcnet-learn }   # name == Service name
subsets:
- addresses: [ { ip: 10.40.0.9 } ]
  ports: [ { port: 80 } ]
```

### Verify
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get svc ext-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}{"\n"}'   # empty
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=ext-svc
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints ext-svc         # 10.40.0.9:80 (aggregated view)
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **The link is the label** `kubernetes.io/service-name=<svc>`, not any reference field — wrong label → Service shows no endpoints.
- Service must have **no selector** (keep `ports`). A selector makes Kubernetes manage endpoints and overwrite yours.
- Port **names** must align between Service and slice (use `""` when the Service port is unnamed).
- Set `addressType` correctly (`IPv4` for an IPv4 address).
- Manual endpoints are **unhealthchecked** — Kubernetes won't detect a dead backend.
- Legacy `Endpoints` object's name must equal the Service name (different binding rule than EndpointSlice).

### Quick reference
```yaml
# selector-less Service: ports, no selector
# EndpointSlice: labels{kubernetes.io/service-name: ext-svc},
#   addressType: IPv4, endpoints[].addresses, ports[].port
```
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=ext-svc
```
